Region: The plain later held by Moab, east of the Dead Sea
History: The Emim were an ancient people of the Moabite plain, remembered as giants. Chedorlaomer defeated them at Shaveh Kiriathaim (Genesis 14:5), and Deuteronomy 2:10-11 explains that the Emim 'were a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakims; which also were accounted giants, as the Anakims.' The Moabites, descended from Lot, inherited the land the Emim had held.
Culture: Known only as a great and tall people of the plain, counted among the Rephaim in Deuteronomy's reckoning.
BibleConnection: The Emim belong to Deuteronomy's lesson that the land's history is a history of displacements: giants held Moab's plain before Moab, just as the Anakim held Canaan before Israel.
